// export-surface.js — A MODULE WHOSE ENTIRE EXPORT SURFACE IS A SPECIFIER LIST.
//
// SCANNED, NEVER RUN, and a file of its own rather than three lines in
// test/fixtures/js-call/alpha.mjs. The reason is measured rather than stylistic.
//
// The entry-surface arm for `export { f }` (rules/js-controlflow.rofl) has a
// site in the call-graph corpus — `export { renamed as exposed }` — and DELETING
// THE ARM COSTS NOTHING THERE. Measured 2026-09-08: `renamed` stays `reachable`
// because `bviaRename` calls it and `bviaRename` is exported inline, so the walk
// arrives from a seed the mutation does not touch. A mutant that survives
// because every path to the answer is doubled is measuring the corpus.
//
// What the arm needs is a function whose ONLY road from a seed is the specifier
// list, and in the runnable corpus that means a function nothing calls at
// runtime — which would put two more names on the census's silent-but-wired
// list for a question that has nothing to do with instrumentation. Here it costs
// one file and no runtime at all.
//
// THE SHAPE:
//   helper   is called by viaList and by nothing else
//   viaList  is exported ONLY through the specifier list below
//   lonely   is exported the same way and called by nobody
//
// With the arm: viaList is an entry point, the walk reaches helper, and
// `may_not_be_reached` is empty. Without it: the file has no entry surface at
// all, `no_entry_point[audit]` fires, and `helper` — a function this module
// exports and calls — is reported maybe-dead. That is the dangerous direction,
// and it is the same one `export_kind_unseen[audit]` exists to catch, arriving
// through a FORM rather than through a misspelling.

function helper(n) {
  return n + 1;
}

function viaList(n) {
  return helper(n);
}

function lonely(n) {
  return n;
}

export { helper as h, viaList as v, lonely as l };
